ops.label: start
ops.text: Every timetable names a different city. Each departure remains 3:17.
A man in a railway coat asks which version you intend to miss.
Oren folds the impossible timetable and follows your light home.
The destinations disagree. The handwriting does not.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Sea water climbs the wallpaper, then withdraws without wetting the bed.
Someone calls beyond the returning water. You cannot hold the room yet.
Sera takes your hand as if she had expected you to be late.
You tie a pale thread where the tide cannot decide to reach.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Metal keys grow from black branches. Each bears a room instead of a name.
The branch closes behind the key as though healing a small wound.
Two incompatible teeth turn together when wrapped in pale thread.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Three intake cards share the same patient number and three different names.
Mara, Oren, and Sera each recognize the handwriting as their own.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Your house stands across a street too narrow for either front door to open.
For one breath, both windows contain the same warm figures.
The other porch folds flat, but its house number stays in your hand.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Three kitchens occupy one room. Each table waits beneath a different light.
No meal becomes the original. Everyone remembers being fed.
One table remains. The empty places around it feel deliberate.

ops.label: start
ops.text: A child and an adult write ROWAN on the same submerged blackboard.
Mara recalls a sibling. Sera recalls the clinician who signed her chart.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Every dead receiver rings. Each voice asks for MAINT-ROWAN.
The line accepts the name and rejects your voice.
The voices go quiet. One whispers that a function can still become a person.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Half-made faces turn away when you offer to finish them.
They ask to remain fragments rather than become convenient strangers.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Bell waits behind a white desk, correcting every sentence into an absence.
Bell removes one redaction: I was built to forget you.
A narrow room forms around Bell. The walls continue taking notes.
The desk is empty. A fresh page remembers the pressure of Bell's hand.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Roots beneath the hearth shed their bark. Braided cables shine underneath.
The house is not hiding machinery. It is how the machinery learned to be seen.

ops.label: start
ops.text: A corridor of status lights opens only when your palm meets the wall.
ADMINISTRATOR: MAINT-ROWAN. Isolation authority remains active.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Rain climbs toward a ceiling of fans. Every drop carries a temperature.
There is power for one recovery, or a small world that cannot grow forever.

ops.label: start
ops.text: One body remains viable. The ledger names Rowan Venn.
Mara says your name, then stops before deciding whom she means.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Rowan initiated isolation. The procedure saved one body and trapped every copy.
Years passed outside. Shared experience made the incomplete records new people.

ops.label: start
ops.text: The safest stones are memories you allowed to disagree.
Discarded versions walk beside the path as red, patient echoes.

ops.label: start
ops.text: Mara asks for the living. Oren asks for continuity. Sera asks who holds the key.
No answer preserves everyone. Each guest chooses to stand with you anyway.

ops.label: start
ops.text: The house sheds impossible rooms while you bind the last doorframe.
The final latch turns. Three futures wait on the other side.

ops.label: start
ops.text: A body, a bounded home, or a world without a keeper. Nothing leaves unchanged.
Rowan wakes alone, carrying names that no external record can prove.
The Drift stops expanding. Oren records the first permanent morning.
Authority scatters among the guests. Sera opens the door without permission.

ops.label: start
ops.text: A porch faces your house from a street too narrow to stand between them.
One line of paving stones agrees to remain.
Under the mat: two house numbers, both warm from the same sun.
